findings.area: Born-scaled rule leaves SHELF IT (95) shelved words below the 12 px floor
findings.evidence: Scratch integrated build /tmp/eos_rev_readability_code_int, 390x844. Script /tmp/rev_read_r2/minw.mjs samples the smallest visible user word (opacity >= .5) every 250 ms during a full play. Result: on `.shelfThoughtBubble.shelved` it was 12.7 px at 19.0 s, then 11.9 px at 20.3 s and still 11.9 px at 23.0 s. The game finished with 0 errors. The cause is lines 959/965: the shelved card was drawn at scale >= .97 first, so it sits in `S.full` and is never compensated. It renders at font x scale. The build report says 'SHELF IT words stay at 16.3-16.6' and '>= 12 px in every game measured', and this run contradicts both. PARK IT (32) is fine (min 16 px). ROUND-2 VERIFICATION OF THE r1 FINDINGS, all fixed: (1) DRAMA MACHINE at 390: both buttons are 13 px on 2 whole lines, rects y 541-583 inside the machine (bottom 602), sw=cw, elementFromPoint hits both. At 1280 both are 14 px, inside the machine, hits OK (screenshot sheet /tmp/rev_read_r2/sheet390.png). (8) ZOOM OUT 30 and MICROSCOPE 58 at 390 and 1280 (/tmp/rev_read_r2/shr*.json): font-size never rises while a word shrinks (ZOOM OUT stays at 16.3; MICROSCOPE stays at 15.3/16.3 down to scale .28-.3). The rendered size rises only when the next word appears; 0 errors, both finished. Minors: cleanup restores and clears the state; state is kept per root in a WeakMap; overlay skip is an explicit list and the walk stops at .releaseStage/.tsArcade; word-fit minimum is 14. Phone HUD keeps LVL always visible, and sparks/tokens/chain show in the hit toast. MIND BEND is visible at play start (31 px tall, 13 px) and hidden after the first hit via .isActive. Legacy POP reveal at 390: card 39-351, PREV/NEXT in one row at y 505-549 with no overlap. Performance: every pass runs in the RO step, so the flush max is 0. HOT POTATO full play at 1280: own p50 0.6 ms, p95 1.1 ms, 1/131 passes over 2 ms, finished in 53 s. No ResizeObserver-loop errors, even with extra shallow ResizeObservers on body/.tsArcade/.releaseStage. 0 page errors, and smallText(12) is empty for POP, DRAMA and HOT POTATO reveal/play.
findings.fix: For an element in S.full that is outside EOS_READ_SHRINK_SEL, once its scale has held for EOS_READ_HOLD_MS, compensate only up to the plain floor: EOS_READ_FLOOR_PX / (sc*k), i.e. 12.5 px rendered, never up to the 16/15 word target. Shrink mechanics stay strictly monotonic through the skip list, and parked or shelved states never fall below 12 px. Another option is an allowlist of static parked states (`.shelfThoughtBubble.shelved`). Re-run minw.mjs on 95 at 390 and 1280, and correct the report's claim.

findings.area: FINGER TRAP (102) user words now render at 13.9-14 px (report says still compensated to 16.2)
findings.evidence: /tmp/rev_read_r2/ft2.mjs at 390 drew the word at 16.3 px x .997 at 1.37 s. Then `.ftTrap` scales to .903 and then .860, giving 13.9 px rendered with data-eos-floor 16.3 and no compensation. /tmp/rev_read_r2/ft.mjs at 1280 measured 16.2 px for about 1.7 s, then 14.0 px (sc .859) from 4.1 s on. The trap tightens after the word was first drawn at full size, so the element is in S.full (line 959) and is skipped at line 965. This is deterministic in a real browser too. The result is >= 12 px, so it is not tiny, but it is below the §4.1 word target of 16 desktop / 15 phone and below the round-1 behaviour. The build report says 'FINGER TRAP's born-scaled .86 tube is still compensated (13.9 → 16.2)', and that did not reproduce.
findings.fix: Either accept this as the cost of the shrink rule and correct the report, or treat `.ftTrap` as a static container: allowlist it for full compensation, or apply the 12.5 px-only compensation above. If you choose full compensation, verify the FINGER TRAP words at 390 and 1280.

findings.area: Reduced motion: phone hit-toast TOKENS/CHAIN still slide with an overshoot
findings.evidence: Line 191: the RM rule `${EOS_A}.stage-play .releaseGameHost .tsShiftRewardHud>*{translate:none!important;transition:none!important}` has specificity (3,4,0). It loses to the base `.tsShiftRewardHud>:is(.token,.chain)` (3,5,0) and to the line-174 `.tsShiftRewardHud.isHit>:is(.token,.chain)` (3,6,0). Those two keep `translate:0 -8px` and `transition: … translate .3s cubic-bezier(.2,1.5,.4,1)`. Measured at 390 with reducedMotion:true, 500 ms after a DRAMA MACHINE hit: token and chain had computed translate '0px -8px', opacity 0, visibility visible, i.e. mid-slide. The spark, whose RM rule has a :has() boost, was static. The build report says 'Reduced motion: no slide'. Round 1 had only a fade here, so this is a small regression in the changed HUD code.
findings.fix: Make the RM override win, for example `${EOS_A}.stage-play .releaseGameHost .tsShiftRewardHud.tsShiftRewardHud.tsShiftRewardHud>*{translate:none!important;transition:none!important}` (>= (3,6,0) and later in the file), or list both the base and the .isHit selectors with an extra class. Verify that the computed translate is 'none' during a hit at 390 with reducedMotion.

findings.area: r1 finding 8 only partly fixed: MICROSCOPE (58) word still grows back while the game shrinks it (word-fit path)
findings.evidence: Builds used: isolated /tmp/eos_rev_readability_experience and integrated /tmp/eos_rev_readability_experience_int. ZOOM OUT (30) is fixed: /tmp/rev_rd2/shrink.mjs ran a full play at 390 and 1280 and found 0 font-size rises while scaled and maxFsGrowth 0. MICROSCOPE is not. Per-frame trace /tmp/rev_rd2/micro2.mjs at 1280, one focus-knob tap every 1.8 s. Each row is t, font px, scale, rendered px, box. Word 1: 14px! at scale .98 (13.7 rendered), then scale .78 (10.9 rendered), then at +330 ms the floor writes 16.25px! and the word renders at 12.8 (box 20 to 23 px wide). Word 2: 14.7 at scale .80 (11.7), then 16.25 at .81 (13.2). Word 3: 15.2 at .80 (12.2), then 16.25 (13.0). So on every word, the first turn of the knob shrinks the thought and it then visibly rebounds by 12-17%. At 390 the full-play sampler found the same rebound on 6 of 6 words (14 to 15.3 px, about +0.4 px rendered). At the start of each word the floor also creeps the size down by itself at full scale (16.25, 15.6, 15.1, 14.7 within about 1 s) before the player acts. Root cause, in the regular pass: `want = eosReadWordFit(el, cs, fs, nat, want, sc * ctx.k)`. Inside the fit, `Math.max(fit, EOS_READ_WORD_FIT_MIN / ratio)` turns the 14 px minimum into 14/.78 = 17.9 px once the game scales the word down. The fitted size is then dropped and the font rises to `want`. Neither the new `S.full` check nor the `.u58` entry in EOS_READ_SHRINK_SEL gates this path; they only gate held-scale compensation. The fix contract was that 'rendered word size must decrease monotonically', and the builder's claim that MICROSCOPE is monotonic does not hold at 100 ms or per-frame sampling.
findings.fix: Pass the game's shrink to the word fit only for boxes the floor compensates. Use `ratio = scaled ? sc * ctx.k : ctx.k`, or equivalently use ctx.k whenever `S.full.has(el) || el.closest(EOS_READ_SHRINK_SEL)`. Also, while sc < .97 on a `full` or shrink-game element that already has a rec, keep `rec.px` (never raise it), the same way the `rec.scaled` hold branch does. To stop the creep at birth, apply the word fit (or skip EOS_READ_WORD_PAD) when the MO path first floors a word inside an object ≤ 220 px, so the size settles in one write. Re-run a per-frame trace of MICROSCOPE at 1280 and 390 with slow taps (1.5-2 s apart). Rendered px must never rise within a word.

findings.area: Phone HUD hit toast (new right-aligned 2-3 pill stack) covers in-arena content for 3.2 s after every hit
findings.evidence:
/tmp/rev_rd2/toast.mjs at 390x844 sets .isHit on ids 100-110. The toast pills sit at x 236-363, y 102-195 on games with a .literalProgress pill (sparks + tokens + chain) and at y 102-162 on the others. Their pointer-events is none, so input is never blocked, but they paint over:
- RAIN OUT 110: the user's word clouds ('yelled', 'at' with PULL TO BREAK)
- id 108: a user word target ('boss')
- DRAMA MACHINE 105: the '0 / 6 TAKES CUT' counter and the TAKE 3 tile (visible in /tmp/rev_rd2/dm390_b_mid.png)
- FINGER TRAP 102: the PUSH arrows row and its '0/5' readout
- VOLUME KNOB 104: the knob readout
In tap-every-second games the toast is up most of the play time. This is not a strict regression: round 1 showed the whole HUD as a centred, full-width wrapped toast in the same band. It still breaks the phone-first 'no overlap' rule on primary targets that carry the user's words.
findings.fix: On phones, show the hit feedback as one compact row: either one combined pill (e.g. '✦ +8 · ×3') beside or over the right end of the meter row, or swap the meter label for about 1.2 s. Do not stack 3 pills down into the arena. Alternatively, shorten the toast to about 1.2 s and give it a translucent backdrop. Re-check 105, 108 and 110 at 390 with a mid-play screenshot.
